systems.name: Inbox → Commitment Ledger
systems.tagline: Every thread that implies an obligation becomes exactly one task, forever, without duplicates.
systems.trigger_mechanism: cron Worker polls Gmail every 30 min (deployed via wrangler — NOT through the Cloudflare connector)
systems.dedupe: unique(source='gmail', source_id=thread_id, target='todoist') — upsert, never insert
systems.weakest_link: Gmail is pull-only: nothing wakes the system when mail lands. The cron is the system. Without it this is a button a human presses.
systems.proof: search_threads for 5 threads read-only; show extracted title + inferred due date + the thread_id that would be stored. Zero writes.
build_plan: Create the crosswalk table in Supabase (un-pause the project first — all 5 are INACTIVE).
Write the Gmail poll as a Cloudflare Worker with a cron trigger; deploy with wrangler.
Worker calls Claude once per batch to classify + extract due dates (the one judgment hop).
Upsert into crosswalk, then create Todoist tasks only for rows that inserted.
Escalate rule: auto-create only for threads matching a narrow filter; everything else lands in a weekly review list.
systems.why_it_wins: Highest certainty payback in the set. Zero send risk because Gmail physically cannot send here. One table, one cron, one judgment hop.

systems.name: Reconciliation Sentinel
systems.tagline: Two systems that should agree, compared nightly. Reports the gap; never touches the money.
systems.dedupe: n/a — read-only up to the digest; the digest is keyed on (period, run_date)
systems.weakest_link: Boundary and rounding mismatch. Two systems closing periods differently manufacture phantom gaps. Normalise period and unit first and state the normalisation inside the report, or the first week of output destroys trust.
systems.proof: Pick one known-good transaction; show it matching on both sides before running a full period.
build_plan: Land both sides into Supabase tables with an explicit period + currency normalisation step.
Deterministic diff in SQL — this rib must never run through Claude.
Claude explains only the anomalies that survive the diff, with the rows attached as evidence.
Post digest to chat with the normalisation stated at the top.
Never auto-correct. Report the diff and let a person decide.
systems.why_it_wins: Money-adjacent, fully deterministic where it matters, and the output is trusted because the system never writes to either source of truth.

systems.name: The Atlas as a Running System
systems.tagline: The map maintains itself: the registry re-derives, verification decays, the graph stays honest.
systems.dedupe: the registry rebuild is idempotent by construction — same dump in, same JSON out
systems.weakest_link: Confidence decay is a policy, not a fact. A VERIFIED profile from six months ago is a DIRECTORY profile wearing a badge — vendors change tools without notice. Pick a half-life and enforce it, or the tier labels rot into decoration.
systems.proof: Re-run engine/graph.py --validate on a schedule; it fails loudly on any key-vocabulary drift, which is exactly the bug class that silently deleted `project` edges before.
build_plan: CI job runs build_registry.py + graph.py --validate on every push; a vocabulary error fails the build.
Weekly job ages every VERIFIED profile toward DOCUMENTED and DOCUMENTED toward DIRECTORY.
Digest names the connectors whose verification expired and which live systems depend on them.
Re-render and republish the map so the picture never drifts from the registry.
systems.why_it_wins: Cheapest system here and the one that keeps every other claim true. The validator alone would have caught the project_name bug that had been silently removing edges from the five most-used connectors.

systems.name: Meeting → CRM → Follow-up Draft
systems.tagline: Every call updates the record and leaves a drafted follow-up waiting, joined on participant email.
systems.trigger_mechanism: cron Worker polls the meetings connector hourly for new transcripts
systems.dedupe: unique(source='meeting', source_id=transcript_id) — one summary, one draft, one task set per call
systems.weakest_link: The email → company hop. Personal-domain attendees (gmail.com) carry no firmographic signal and one human often has two addresses. Degrade to 'unmatched' rather than guessing the account.
systems.proof: Pull one past transcript; show a participant email resolving to an existing CRM contact before anything is written.
build_plan: Crosswalk table: transcript_id → crm_contact_id → draft_id.
Worker polls transcripts, sends text to Claude for summary + commitment extraction.
Resolve participants by email against CRM; unmatched participants queue for human review, never auto-create.
Write CRM note (mutate — confirmed policy), create Gmail draft (safe), create Todoist tasks.
Never send. The draft is the deliverable.
systems.why_it_wins: The meetings archetype is the single richest enrichment source in the directory — it turns speech into email-keyed structured data, which is the strongest join key there is.

systems.name: Personal Operating System
systems.tagline: The whole connected stack, working as one thing, on the connectors already authorised.
systems.trigger_mechanism: cron Worker — deployed via wrangler, since the Cloudflare connector cannot deploy Workers
systems.dedupe: one crosswalk keyed on (source_system, source_id, target_system)
systems.weakest_link: The calendar. Google Calendar here exposes only semantic search_events — the morning digest cannot enumerate today's events, it can only search for terms it guesses. Every other rib is solid; this one degrades to 'search for likely meeting keywords' which is genuinely worse than a human glancing at the calendar. Either accept the degradation or add a calendar connector that can list.
systems.proof: Everything in this system is VERIFIED — all 8 core connectors had schemas loaded and Supabase answered a live read-only call this session. Run the digest rib read-only and compare its output against the actual calendar and inbox.
build_plan: Un-pause a Supabase project first — all five are INACTIVE, and the spine cannot run paused.
Deploy one cron Worker via wrangler. This is the single piece that turns everything else from on-demand into automatic.
Build the digest rib first: read-only, zero risk, immediate daily value.
Inbox → tasks second, with the crosswalk. Gmail cannot send, so the risk ceiling is 'a wrong task got created'.
Materialize rib third: analysis → Canva/Drive, moving bytes by URL.
Weekly review reads the spine's own tables — the closure.
systems.why_it_wins: The only system here that is entirely VERIFIED rather than DIRECTORY — every connector in it was schema-checked this session. It is the one to build first, because it is the one whose claims are all provable today.

systems.name: Support Signal → Roadmap
systems.tagline: Voice-of-customer collapsed into themes with verbatim evidence, weekly, into the backlog.
systems.weakest_link: The semantic join. Theme clustering is inference, not measurement. Show verbatim quotes under every theme so a human can overrule it, and never present inferred clusters as counts of fact.
systems.proof: Show 3 themes with the verbatim quotes behind each before creating a single backlog item.
build_plan: Land tickets + reviews into one table with source provenance preserved.
Weekly: Claude clusters into themes, each carrying its source row IDs.
Persist themes with a stable slug so week-over-week movement is measurable.
Create/refresh one backlog item per theme above a volume threshold.
Post the movement (new / growing / fading) to chat — the delta is the product, not the list.
systems.why_it_wins: Turns the weakest key in the system (free text) into a tracked, dated series. Cold start is real — it needs ~2 weeks before the deltas mean anything.

economics.assumptions: build @ $60/h, reclaimed time @ $45/h — ASSUMED, tune in WEIGHTS

systems.name: Deploy → Changelog → Fan-out
systems.tagline: Shipping writes its own changelog, its own asset, and its own draft announcement.
systems.trigger_mechanism: GitHub deployment webhook — a genuine event trigger, not a poll
systems.weakest_link: Partial fan-out. Three of four sinks land and the fourth silently doesn't. Report per-sink status; never report 'done' for the whole fan.
systems.proof: Run against the last real deployment; compare the generated changelog against the actual commit diff before wiring any sink.
build_plan: Webhook receiver (Worker) captures deployment_id + commit range.
Claude writes the changelog from the diff — the one judgment hop.
Materialize into a doc; push the doc URL, not the bytes, everywhere downstream.
Canva: upload-asset-from-url only accepts already-public URLs — check this before designing the rib.
Every outbound is a DRAFT. Nothing here announces anything by itself.
systems.why_it_wins: One of the few designs with a real event trigger rather than a poll. Note Vercel's buy_* tools are in this connector — keep them out of the automated path entirely.

systems.name: Solo-Operator Revenue Cockpit
systems.tagline: One spine, seven independent ribs. Every number that matters, reconciled nightly, in one place.
systems.trigger_mechanism: one nightly cron on the spine drives all deterministic ribs; the weekly Materialize rib runs Sunday
systems.dedupe: per-rib: (source_system, source_id, target) unique in one shared crosswalk table
systems.weakest_link: Auth surface. Twelve accounts is twelve things that can expire, rate-limit, or change plan tier. Ribs are independent so one dying does not kill the cockpit — but nothing tells you it died unless you build the staleness check. Build that first, not last.
systems.proof: Prove one rib end to end (payments ⨝ accounting on a single known invoice) before building the second. Seven ribs proved one at a time is a system; seven ribs built at once is a diagram.
build_plan: Week 1: spine only — Supabase schema, one crosswalk table, nightly cron Worker, staleness monitor, chat delivery.
Week 2-4: one rib per two days, cheapest and most deterministic first (reconcile, then funnel, then fulfilment).
Judgment ribs (churn risk, meeting notes, weekly deck) go last — they are the expensive ones and they depend on accumulated state.
Deterministic ribs run as SQL on the scheduler. Claude touches only the three judgment ribs.
The weekly deck reads the spine's own tables — this is the feedback closure that makes it a system rather than a report.
systems.why_it_wins: The rib architecture is the whole point: 18 connectors, no chain longer than 4 hops, one place state lives, one place output lands. Failure is contained per rib.

systems.name: Hiring Pipeline Machine
systems.tagline: Sourcing to signed offer, with the interview record as the join key.
systems.trigger_mechanism: daily cron + webhook on application received
systems.dedupe: unique(candidate_email, req_id) — the whole pipeline keys on candidate email
systems.weakest_link: Google Calendar exposes only semantic search_events in this stack — it cannot enumerate availability or create an invite. The scheduling rib needs a different calendar connector or a scheduling vendor (Calendly), or it does not exist. This is a VERIFIED blocker, not a guess.
systems.proof: Resolve one past candidate from application through to offer using only email as the join; show every artifact matching.
build_plan: Candidate table keyed on email is the spine — resolve every weak key (name) to email at intake.
Interview transcripts → structured scorecards is the highest-value judgment rib; build it second.
Scheduling requires a calendar connector with write capability — verify BEFORE designing the rib.
Offer/signature rib is irreversible and gets per-action confirmation without exception.
Bias note: keep Claude on summarisation and structure, not on ranking candidates.
systems.why_it_wins: Demonstrates the verification discipline paying off — the scheduling rib would have been designed on an assumption that the connected calendar can write. It cannot.

systems.name: Risk & Compliance Radar
systems.tagline: 119 read-only sensors watching for the thing that ends the company.
systems.trigger_mechanism: daily cron; sanctions and breach feeds hourly
systems.dedupe: unique(sensor_id, subject_key, finding_hash) — a finding is reported once until it changes
systems.weakest_link: Alert fatigue is the failure mode, not missed signal. 119 sensors will generate more findings than any human will read, and a radar nobody reads is worse than none because it manufactures false confidence. The materiality rib is the entire product — everything else is plumbing.
systems.proof: Run the materiality judgment against 30 days of historical findings and check what it would have escalated against what actually mattered. If the precision is bad, the mesh is a liability.
build_plan: Findings table with a stable finding_hash so the same issue is not re-reported daily.
Every sensor is read-only and independent — this archetype set was chosen because none of it can write.
The materiality rib runs Claude against the findings delta with an explicit written threshold.
Escalate above the threshold; everything else accumulates silently and is reviewed weekly.
Note identity_verification only became a usable archetype after the routing fix — it had zero members before.
systems.why_it_wins: The one mesh where the judgment rib is worth more than all the sensors combined — and the design makes that explicit rather than hiding it.

economics.assumptions: build @ $60/h, reclaimed time @ $45/h — ASSUMED, tune in WEIGHTS

systems.name: Market Omniscience Mesh
systems.tagline: 205 read-only sensors on one spine. Blast radius zero. This is what 150+ connectors is actually for.
systems.trigger_mechanism: tiered cron — tick data hourly, fundamentals daily, research weekly
systems.dedupe: unique(sensor_id, entity_key, captured_at) — every sensor writes the same shape
systems.weakest_link: Nobody needs 205 sensors. The design is correct and the marginal sensor is near-worthless — value saturates somewhere around 20-30 well-chosen sources. What this system proves is the *architecture*: that read-only fan-in scales without compounding risk. Treat 205 as the ceiling you can safely approach, not the target you should hit.
systems.proof: Add sensors 1, 2 and 3; confirm each writes the normalised shape and that killing sensor 2 does not affect 1 or 3. That independence is the entire claim — prove it at N=3, and N=205 follows by induction.
build_plan: One normalised observation table: (sensor_id, entity_key, metric, value, unit, captured_at, source_url). Every sensor conforms; no sensor gets a bespoke schema.
One adapter per sensor, each independently deployable and independently killable.
A sensor registry table with a staleness threshold per sensor — the mesh reports its own health, which is what makes degradation self-healing rather than silent.
Claude never touches raw sensor output. It reads the correlation table only.
Add sensors in order of marginal information gain, and stop when the brief stops changing.
systems.why_it_wins: The honest answer to 'can a system benefit from 150+ connectors'. Yes — but only in this topology. Every rib is read-only and independent, so failure is additive, not multiplicative. A 200-sensor mesh has a smaller blast radius than a 7-hop write chain.

systems.name: Competitive Intelligence Desk
systems.tagline: Everything published about your market, collapsed into what changed since yesterday.
systems.dedupe: unique(entity_domain, metric, captured_at) — snapshot table; the delta is computed, never stored twice
systems.weakest_link: Cost, and it is not the tokens. This tier of market-data and SEO connectors carries four-figure monthly subscription floors. The run cost line above is dominated by vendor licences, and that number is ASSUMED — verify before committing. A cheaper version using only Exa + Tavily + one SEO source captures most of the value.
systems.proof: Snapshot three competitor domains for two consecutive days; confirm the delta table shows only real movement and no phantom churn from vendor-side rounding.
build_plan: Snapshot-and-diff is the whole architecture. Store daily snapshots, compute deltas, never store the delta.
All sensor ribs are read-only and independent — add sources without touching existing ones.
Browser automation is the last-resort rib for sources with no API; treat its output as untrusted input.
Claude writes only the brief, from the delta table — never from raw sensor output.
Start with three sources and add one per week; the brief must stay under a page or it stops being read.
systems.why_it_wins: Pure fan-in on read-only sensors, so it scales safely — but it is the clearest case where the binding constraint is vendor licence cost, not engineering.

systems.name: Client Delivery Factory
systems.tagline: Intake to invoice as one tracked object — the agency operating system.
systems.trigger_mechanism: form submission webhook starts the object; each stage transition fires the next rib
systems.dedupe: one `engagement` row is the spine object; every artifact carries engagement_id. Naming convention `client-project-YYYYMMDD` across Drive, Linear and Canva turns the weak `project` key into a strong one.
systems.weakest_link: Two irreversible hops in the automated path — sending for signature and issuing an invoice. Both are commitment-grade. These get a fresh in-chat yes every time, or a hard whitelist with a value ceiling. Plan approval is not send approval.
systems.proof: Run one historical engagement through end to end in dry-run mode: every artifact generated, nothing sent, nothing invoiced. Compare against what actually happened.
build_plan: Define the engagement object and the naming convention FIRST — it is what makes `project` a strong join key across six tools.
Build intake → CRM → project as one rib; prove it before touching money.
Documents and decks are Materialize ribs; move bytes by URL, never through context.
Signature and invoice ribs ship LAST, behind explicit confirmation, with a value ceiling.
The digest rib reads the spine and closes the loop.
systems.why_it_wins: The naming convention is the highest-leverage line in the whole design: it costs nothing but discipline and converts the weakest join key into the strongest across six systems at once.

systems.name: Maximum Safe Mesh — the 293 ceiling
systems.tagline: Every read-only connector in the directory, at once. The hard upper bound on a zero-risk system.
systems.weakest_link: This is a boundary object, not a build. It exists to answer 'how far does this go' with a number derived from the registry rather than from imagination: 293 connectors carry side_effects=read, so 293 is the largest system that cannot break anything it touches. The 294th connector is a write, and the moment you add it the blast-radius argument collapses and you are back to designing chains.
systems.proof: The claim is structural, not empirical: query the registry for side_effects='read' and count. engine/graph.py reports it as read_only_ceiling.
build_plan: Not a build plan — a bound. Use it to decide where a real mesh should stop.
The practical lesson: pick the 20-30 sensors whose marginal information is highest and stop there.
The structural lesson: read-only breadth is free; write depth is expensive. Design accordingly.
systems.why_it_wins: It is the only number in this whole exercise that is a fact about the directory rather than a judgment about a design.
